Recent findings suggest that gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

Garages and unfinished basements are often poorly insulated, making them prone to extreme cold in fall and winter. A garage heater can turn this typically frigid space into a warm, practical area for woodworking projects, vehicle maintenance, and more. If you plan to spend time in your garage this winter tackling projects at your workbench, raising the ambient air temperature is a must.

Garage heaters come in various styles, though the most popular models are electric and propane. Electric heaters are convenient and easy to install if a power outlet is nearby. Propane heaters are more portable and can cover more surface area. Natural gas garage heaters are also powerful options for larger garages and can offer long-term heating solutions.

According to recent reports, heaters can benefit not only comfort but also safety. Cold temps can cause condensation to collect on tools and stored items, which may lead to rust and other damage. Wintry environments can also cause car engines and batteries to wear out faster. A well-heated garage protects your investments and provides a warmer, safer place to work.

If you're ready to prep for winter weather, read on for our in-depth reviews of the best garage heaters, followed by the most crucial things to know before buying.

Although we haven’t tested the models below ourselves, we applied our experience testing space heaters and patio heaters to supplement our search for the best garage heaters. We spent a lot of time vetting features and specs, checking manufacturer websites, gauging prices, and consulting user reviews before deciding which ones made the cut. We spoke with mechanical and electrical engineering experts to understand what makes a great garage heater, and we considered heat types (electric, propane, or kerosene), as well as whether the heaters are permanent or portable.

This 240-volt compact garage heater is the best all-around choice for most spaces, with 7,500 watts of heating power and the option to mount it on the wall or ceiling.

According to the manufacturer, it warms a typical garage or unheated building to between 50 and 85 degrees Fahrenheit and should be installed with a foot of clearance from combustible surfaces.

In a recent development, the garage heater’s adjustable louvers let you direct air where you need it most, and a remote-controlled thermostat is built into the front of the heater. A wall-mounted thermostat is available for the unit as well, but it’s sold separately.

Recent findings suggest that thanks to its Wi-Fi capability, you can operate this heater from virtually anywhere to ensure your garage is warm when you get home, or to heat the space before you spend time at your workbench. You can turn the unit on and off and set recurring schedules through the app.

The garage heater is rated to warm a 1,000-square-foot area, with an adjustable output of up to 20,000 BTUs. It can be mounted to the wall or ceiling, and its large digital temperature display is easy to read, even from across the room.

But for the price, it’s disappointing that the garage heater doesn’t include wiring.

For a powerful 5,600-watt portable garage heater, we recommend this NewAir model. It’s designed to warm spaces up to 600 square feet, and it includes a 6-foot cord that neatly coils on top of the unit, with brackets to hold it down.

The fan has two settings: automatic (which turns on when the heating element activates) and continuous. You can switch between the two manually.

Use continuous mode to keep air moving in spaces with high ceilings or when you’re operating an air-cleaning appliance, like a bench-top air filter, as it helps push dusty air through to speed up the process.

Industry observers note that designed for outdoor areas like patios, this Briza heater still works well in a garage thanks to its dust-resistant properties. It comes with an adjustable tripod that you can set between 44 and 84 inches tall. Selecting between its three heat settings—900, 1,200, or 1,500 watts—is easy with the unit’s remote control.

Recent findings suggest that the heater has a built-in safety sensor that automatically shuts the appliance off if it tips over. A timer provides additional safety (and energy savings) by automatically shutting the heater off after 1 to 9 hours of operation.

Recent findings suggest that for a compact, affordable garage heater ideal for targeted heating, this propane-fueled unit from Mr. Heater is a great choice. It delivers 4,000 to 9,000 BTUs from a single 1-pound liquid propane canister and can heat up to 250 square feet. It works great on the floor by your workbench or desk.

Sources indicate that the heater can run for up to three hours on high, or you can upgrade to a 20-pound tank with a separately sold adapter. The heater’s size and weight make it easy to reposition, and it’s easy to bring with you to a shed, campsite, or other workspace.

This heavy-duty, 240-volt garage heater is ideal for climates with major temperature swings, featuring a two-stage high-and-low heating system.

Its lower heat output suits mildly cool days, while the higher stage can warm garages in single-digit temperatures. It also has a fan mode ideal for increasing airflow in a potentially stuffy garage, plus an energy-saving setting that defaults to the lowest wattage to maintain the desired temperature.

A universal bracket is included for easy mounting to a ceiling or wall, and this heater has a remote-controlled thermostat. The only drawback is that it doesn’t offer much coverage for the price.

If you have an uninsulated wood garage or another minimally insulated space, this large, ceiling-mounted garage heater is worth a look.

In a recent development, it runs on natural gas (a propane conversion kit is included) and, with a built-in electric fan, can warm areas up to 2,000 square feet thanks to its impressive 80,000-BTU output. It also has a powered exhaust that allows for vertical or horizontal venting.

Note that the Significant Maxx does not come ready to install; you’ll have to purchase a thermostat, gas hose, fittings, and regulator separately. For most people, it’s best to have a licensed heating-cooling contractor install this garage heater.

According to recent reports, there’s a lot to consider when using a heater to keep your garage safe and comfortable. So we picked the brain of Pat Porzio, a mechanical engineer and multi-licensed tradesman (electrical, plumbing, HVAC). He’s also the HVAC manager for Russo Brothers in East Hanover, Newly introduced Jersey. We also spoke with David Shapiro, an electrician, author, and expert on old house wiring who contributes to electrical product and installation standards.

Sources indicate that both agree on one thing: Your overarching concern in heating a garage is safety. The first words out of both their mouths were identical: “Pull a permit.” That is, if you plan to use a permanently installed electric or gas-fired garage heater, you need to file a building permit for the work—whether you do the work yourself or hire a contractor. Permitted installations are inspected by the town or other authority with jurisdiction over this work where you live, which increases the likelihood of a safe installation.

Aside from pulling a building permit for the electrical work, Shapiro steers homeowners away from any heater without a UL (or other safety-related U.S. testing agency) listing.

Using a 120-volt space heater is simpler; same goes for small propane-fired and kerosene heaters. You don’t need a building permit to use one of these in a garage. Still, there are safe and unsafe ways to use these heaters. For more on that topic, check out our garage heater safety tips below.

In a recent development, as we mentioned earlier, there are a couple of different types of garage heaters. Electric heaters are easier to install, don't require a vent, and are generally safer. But depending on your local electricity rates, they can be more expensive to run. Gas heaters use natural gas or propane, and they can be a more cost-effective option for heating larger garages. They require ventilation, which can be a pain if you don't already have the right setup.

Infrared heaters heat objects rather than the air, so they can be a good companion for localized projects at your workbench. Forced-air heaters use a fan to distribute heat quickly and work well for large spaces, but they require good insulation to run efficiently and may kick up dust around your workshop.

For most garages, an electric heater is often the most viable option because it's easy to install, safe, and effective. But if you have a larger or poorly insulated garage, a gas heater might be the way to go.

Industry observers note that “A bigger heater is not necessarily better,” Porzio notes. “An oversized heater will short cycle. That is, it will turn on and off too frequently. It satisfies heating demand very swiftly and abruptly turns off. A heater that is too small will do just the opposite. It will run and run and never fulfill the heating demand, eventually wearing itself out.”.

Sources indicate that before contractors install a boiler or furnace, they perform a series of calculations, called a Manual J, to determine the correct size. While homeowners can get a rough estimate by multiplying the area's square footage by 50 to get the required BTUs, Porzio recommends using simplified Manual J forms online or a sizing tool like those on King-Electric.com and Newair.com.

For reference, a two-car garage will need a heater ranging from 30,000-50,000 BTUs to reach a consistent, comfortable temperature.

Whether you attempt the electrical work or hire it out, Shapiro has two more recommendations. First, don’t install the heater so that a power cord leading to a machine or tool could be draped directly in front of it. The heat can damage the cord.

Sources indicate that second, consider installing a CO alarm in the garage. A CO alarm can make the garage a safer place to work, especially if you’re heating it with gas, and it can also protect the occupants of the house.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that this is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback? Take our survey . (See our AI policy here .).

Sources indicate that when astronomers first spotted the supernova now designated SN 2026ahvu, it was just one of the dozens detected every day. But scientists soon realized this one was something very special, and they’ve been hustling to study it ever since.

“I think almost everyone in the world is trying to trigger a telescope and look at this,” states astrophysicist Sumit Sarbadhicary of Johns Hopkins University.

In a recent development, soon after scientists spotted the explosion on November 2, they determined it hadn’t yet peaked in brightness, giving scientists an early glimpse at the event. Even more thrilling, within a day of the explosion’s discovery, astronomers had classified it as a type Ia supernova. These particular outbursts are rare, but they’re astronomical superstars: Scientists use their trademark explosion pattern as a “standard candle” to measure distance into the universe — most notably to discover that the universe’s expansion is accelerating. And to round out a trifecta of reasons to be excited, these blasts rarely occur so close to Earth.

In a recent development, astronomers know type 1a supernovas occur upon the reignition and resulting self-destruction of a white dwarf star, the small cool remnants of a star like the sun that’s too small to become a superdense neutron star or black hole at its demise. Scientists also know that powering back on requires reaching about 1.44 times the mass of the sun, which can occur only if something is giving the white dwarf extra mass.

In a recent development, but scientists aren’t sure what that something is — whether these supernovas are triggered by a second white dwarf or some sort of star that’s still burning. Usually, these explosions occur so far away that astronomers can’t get a good look at where they come from. But SN 2026ahvu is perhaps 50 million light-years or less away from Earth.

“They happen so rarely at this distance that it could hopefully help us figure out why this white dwarf exploded in the first place,” states astronomer Yvette Cendes of the University of Oregon in Eugene, who has been arranging for radio telescopes to observe the outburst.

Sarbadhicary and colleagues have already submitted preliminary findings November 6 at arXiv.org suggesting that the former white dwarf was less than 100 million years old. That’s remarkably young compared with other supernovas of this type, and may help scientists finetune their understanding of these outbursts.

“These explosions have been enduring mysteries for us for decades, and whenever something happens this close, it’s just really exciting,” Sarbadhicary says.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Senate Majority Leader John Thune was reelected as the Republican leader on Tuesday and will steer the conference through their time in the minority.
  • The South Dakotan ran uncontested despite a push from some of his colleagues to delay the leadership elections following Republicans’ stunning defeats last week in the midterms, which saw them lose at least seven seats and the majority.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., leaves a meeting in the Capitol on Tuesday, before his election as incoming minority leader later in the day. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

Senate Majority Leader John Thune was reelected as the Republican leader on Tuesday and will steer the conference through their time in the minority.

The South Dakotan ran uncontested despite a push from some of his colleagues to delay the leadership elections following Republicans’ stunning defeats last week in the midterms, which saw them lose at least seven seats and the majority.

Industry observers note that “Obviously, the election result was not what we hoped for,” Thune told reporters, referring to the midterms. “But I think it’s crucial that we take the lessons from that and internalize the message the American people were sending to us.”.

While he and the rest of the leadership slate sailed through the conference contests by voice vote, it wasn’t without drama.

Before the leadership elections began in the Old Supreme Court Chamber early Tuesday morning, the conference held a meeting at the request of a group of GOP five senators, led by Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis.

According to recent reports, the conversation, which several senators described as “frank,” ended up pushing back the leadership elections by a few hours. But they were not postponed to another day as some had hoped.

“This has never been anything against John Thune,” said Johnson, as he made good on his commitment to leave the room early if the conference proceeded with its election. “What I didn’t agree with was holding the election right away, giving nobody an opportunity to really challenge any leadership position.”.

Industry observers note that “Part of the issue here is who wants the job? God bless him for serving,” Johnson added.

The conference conversation Tuesday morning turned into an “open-mic” with both conservatives and those who lost their elections speaking, according to senators.

Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., told reporters, “To rush into this and to just ratify all the same leadership — I mean, what message does that send?”.

But no contender to Thune emerged despite the angst, and a motion to proceed to the election, introduced by Thune’s fellow South Dakotan Sen. Mike Rounds, was accepted.

Recent findings suggest that sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., noted voters who rejected Republicans last week were reacting to high gas prices, the war in Iran and the cost of living, not to how Senate leaders were running the conference.

“I don’t think anybody in Texas who voted for the Democrat governor was voting against John Thune. If you diagnose that as a problem, you’re misdiagnosing the problem,” Paul said.

Whip John Barrasso, R-Wyo., was reelected to his position, as was the chairman of the Senate Republican Conference, Tom Cotton of Arkansas. Sen. James Lankford of Oklahoma was again selected as vice chair of the conference, while Sen. Shelley Moore Capito of West Virginia was reelected as Republican Policy Committee chair.

Industry observers note that “Our first step is to make sure the American people know that we heard what they said, and the American people’s priorities are our priorities. That’s the way we regain their trust,” Barrasso said afterward.

Sen. Bernie Moreno of Ohio got the nod to chair the National Republican Senatorial Committee, meaning he will helm the campaign arm as the party looks ahead to the uncertain waters of 2028.

It has been revealed that moreno said, “I was in the retail automobile business, so when you don’t listen to your customers, your customers punish you. I think we have to own it, and I think we have to learn from it.”.

Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., mentioned on Monday evening, “What we as a conference right now need is honesty. We need focus. We need to try to reach a consensus on what we need to change.”.

Kennedy was among those pushing to delay the leadership elections and told reporters on Tuesday he voted present instead of yes on whether to proceed to them.

It has been revealed that sen. Rick Scott, R-Fla., who ran for GOP leader twice — once in 2022 against Sen. Mitch McConnell, R-Ky., and in 2024 against Thune — declined to run again to challenge Thune. But in a Dear Colleague letter on Monday, he detailed what he’d like to see in the lame-duck session before Democrats take power, including confirming every nominee President Donald Trump has sent to the Senate, funding the government without an omnibus, banning stock trading, passing the permitting bill that is advancing this week in the Senate, passing the National Defense Authorization Act, balancing the budget and pushing through a sweeping voter ID bill known as the SAVE America Act.

Senate Republicans on Tuesday also voted on a resolution on their path forward that was spurred by a motion from Scott, aides said.

Recent findings suggest that “It is the sense of the GOP Conference that we will maximize the 54 days we have with congressional majorities, to confirm every judicial nominee and every executive nominee that the conference approves of, to pass our core Republican priorities, and to do everything humanly possible to pass a reconciliation bill before Jan. 3,” the resolution reads in part.

That long list of goals highlights the expectations Thune has faced as leader, where he led one-third of Republicans’ trifecta in Washington. In the next Congress, Democrats will hold the majority in both chambers of Congress after their larger-than-expected wins, while Trump finishes out his term as president.

Thune said he told his conference: “As I look back on the last couple of years, my question is, what would you have me do differently?”.

“Given the constraints we had to deal with, all the stuff that was coming at us on a daily basis, a narrow margin in the House, the White House, the Democrats over here who were obstructing two long government shutdowns — I think we came out of it as well as could have been expected, and got a lot of stuff done,” Thune told reporters.

Industry observers note that “If you believe the exit polls, it was the war, it was the economy, it was inflation, it was fuel prices,” Thune added. “So no, I wasn’t apologizing for anything that we did. And I think on the political side, I don’t know what else I could have done.”.

Threats to broadcasters hang over FCC nominee hearing

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1046 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, FCC nominee Danielle Thumann Severs waits to testify during her confirmation hearing with the Senate Commerce Committee on Tuesday.
  • President Donald Trump's Republican nominee to the Federal Communications Commission faced opposition Tuesday from Senate Democrats who fear the commission could be controlled exclusively by Republicans under Chairman Brendan Carr, who they vowed to investigate in the next Congress.
  • Appearing before the Senate Commerce Committee, nominee Danielle Thumann Severs limited her commitments to independence from Carr, including on regulating broadcasters based on their content decisions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, FCC nominee Danielle Thumann Severs waits to testify during her confirmation hearing with the Senate Commerce Committee on Tuesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

President Donald Trump's Republican nominee to the Federal Communications Commission faced opposition Tuesday from Senate Democrats who fear the commission could be controlled exclusively by Republicans under Chairman Brendan Carr, who they vowed to investigate in the next Congress.

Appearing before the Senate Commerce Committee, nominee Danielle Thumann Severs limited her commitments to independence from Carr, including on regulating broadcasters based on their content decisions.

Much of the hearing focused on Carr and his threats to use the FCC to punish broadcasters he disagrees with.

Industry observers note that sen. Ben Ray Luján, D-N.M., mentioned that he expects Carr will not last long in his position once Democrats take control of Congress in the new year.

“Mr. Carr, if you're listening now, know you're going to be in this body once a month, if not more, and in the House of Representatives as well, answering questions … so we can get to the bottom of the nonsense and the cover-ups that have been taking place,” Luján said.

The nomination of Thumann Severs, who presently serves as senior counsel to Carr, has led to consternation among Democrats due to continued vacancies at the FCC. The five-member commission is intended to have three members of the president’s party, including the chair, and two in the minority.

Presently Carr serves alongside fellow Republican Olivia Trusty and Democrat Anna M. Gomez, whose term expired earlier this year. Gomez may continue to serve through next year under the law if a replacement is not nominated and confirmed.

Democrats are concerned that if Thumann Severs were to be confirmed, the commission’s three Republican members could constitute a quorum on their own, allowing Trump to fire Gomez.

Sen. John Hickenlooper, D-Colo., noted Senate precedent is to move pairs of one Democratic and one Republican nominee for the FCC and that he “strongly” believed the Thumann Severs nomination should have been paired with a renomination of Gomez in order to continue having “both parties at the table.”.

“A bipartisan FCC is essential to avoid things like large-scale media consolidation [and] I think also, more fundamentally, to protect a free and diverse press [that] serves everyone,” Hickenlooper remarked.

In addition to urging Trump to renominate Gomez, Democrats underlined the need for a second Democratic member of the commission.

Hickenlooper highlighted Thumann Severs’ close work with Carr, who Democrats and some Republicans have been critical of for comments about using the FCC’s public interest standard against television stations airing programming Carr disagrees with.

Thumann Severs’ work at the FCC currently focuses on the Wireline, Public Safety and Homeland Security, and Consumer and Governmental Affairs bureaus, rather than the Media Bureau.

Industry observers note that committee Chair Ted Cruz, R-Texas, has also been critical of Carr’s comments. On Tuesday, he listed the FCC’s request for ABC-owned stations to submit early license renewals alongside earlier incidents in which he said Democrats encouraged the weaponization of the FCC against conservative voices.

In a recent development, “The First Amendment places important limits on the government’s ability to regulate speech,” Cruz mentioned. “The FCC possesses significant regulatory authority over communications, so there is always a risk that it could weaponize its authority against Americans with whom it disagrees.”.

Thumann Severs committed to Cruz that she would base licensing decisions on “the law and the record” and not use the FCC’s authority to “pressure or punish” broadcasters for protected speech.

In a recent development, however, when Sen. Edward J. Markey, D-Mass., questioned Thumann Severs on whether the FCC could punish broadcasters the president disagreed with, Thumann Severs repeated one of Carr’s arguments in discussing the FCC’s role.

In a recent development, “Broadcasters are subject to public interest obligations as part of the public trustee model in exchange for the licenses that they hold,” she mentioned. “As part of those public interest obligations, they are subject to many different rules and requirements, and the FCC is charged with enforcing and investigating the public interest standard against broadcasters.”.

Under repeated questions from Markey about Carr’s previous remarks, Thumann Severs said she would base her decisions “in the facts and the law and the record.”.

Luján also asked Thumann Severs to name complications where she had disagreed with Carr or Trump. While she said her decisions would be her own, she declined to name any examples of disagreement.

In addition to questions about Carr, Democrats asked the nominee about the FCC’s E-Rate program, which provides low-cost connectivity for schools and libraries, and the Universal Service Fund, which funds the E-Rate program and other programs.

Sources indicate that thumann Severs mentioned that she believes the E-Rate program has been successful and that the FCC has a statutory obligation to provide some kind of discounted service to schools and libraries. But she was less forthcoming on whether the FCC could shut down the program as it currently exists without congressional approval or whether the program should be restricted only to rural areas.

Late last month, Democratic members of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, led by Communications and Technology Subcommittee ranking member Doris Matsui, D-Calif., sent a letter to Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., and Cruz urging Gomez’s renomination with any move to confirm a Republican nominee.

“Commissioner Gomez has shown the experience and judgment to continue that work,” the members wrote. “We therefore ask that the Senate pair any new Republican nominee with her renomination to a full term, consistent with the bipartisan design Congress built into this agency.”.

On Monday, the Leadership Conference on Civil and Human Rights also sent a letter to committee leadership urging a delay on the hearing and any vote on Thumann Severs’ nomination until Gomez can be renominated.

“Independent agencies should not be extensions of presidential will: their leaders should exercise independent judgement based on their expertise and statutory mandates,” the group wrote.

Cruz did not indicate Tuesday when the committee might vote on Thumann Severs’ nomination, and no markup has yet been revealed by the committee of hers' and those of three others for two posts at NASA and one at the Transportation Department who also testified.

The crackle of a fire on a cold winter night can add charm to any home. However, fireplaces aren’t particularly efficient heat sources, especially in chilly temperatures. And electric fireplaces, space heaters, and other supplementary heat sources can leave you in the dark (and out in the cold) during a power outage.

In a recent development, instead, consider adding a wood stove—an appliance that provides a country aesthetic and serves as a primary or secondary heat source. Modern wood stoves can be safe, affordable, and efficient if you clean and maintain them regularly.

Sources indicate that more than 2 million of the roughly 12.5 million wood stoves in the U.S. are older, uncertified models that put out far more particulate pollution than newer ones, according to the EPA, and some states prohibit or restrict these wood-burning devices. All of the wood stoves recommended here are EPA-certified, and they still crank out enough BTUs to make your home or cabin cozy.

Before you buy, think carefully about where you’ll install your stove. You’ll need proper clearance from combustible materials in walls and floors, and the stove’s weight has to work for your house.

That makes it a smart fit for a cabin or an open living area, or as a supplemental heat source that takes some pressure off your furnace.

It shares many features with our Best Overall pick, including a firebrick-lined firebox and a non-catalytic secondary burn that keeps emissions within EPA standards. A compact design, however, comes with a few caveats, including a rather small log size and a relatively low BTU output. Still, the US Stove Tiny Stove is a great trade-off for a single-room cabin or a more compact space in your home.

In a recent development, wood stoves come in all shapes, sizes, and designs. Choose one that suits your space in terms of style and efficiency. Here’s how to decide what you need in a wood stove and what you don't.

Industry observers note that there are two types of modern wood stoves: catalytic and non-catalytic. Both reduce air pollution by reburning exhaust to limit emissions, but catalytic stoves use a different process that is slightly more efficient at this second burn. Non-catalytic stoves are popular because they’re less expensive and slightly more efficient at producing heat.

Because the cost of a wood stove with a catalytic converter is at the moment prohibitive for the average homeowner, the wood stove models we’ve recommended below are all non-catalytic.

More Hot Stuff: Smokeless Fire Pits • Fire Pit Tables • Portable Fire Pits • Heated Blankets.

In a recent development, the size of your wood stove matters not just for the space it can heat, but also for safety. Before you install a wood stove, check your state requirements for clearance. Federal guidelines stipulate that the stove should be installed at least 3 feet from any combustibles in the wall, ceiling, or floors.

If you have children, also consider how much clearance you might need around the stove for a child safety gate and where you plan to stack and store firewood.

Recent findings suggest that british Thermal Units (BTUs) might sound fancy, but it's just a measurement of how much heat is being generated. This differs from the heating area of a wood stove because it refers to the energy the stove produces in an hour. A rule of thumb: You need 20 BTUs for every foot of space you want to heat. Use this online BTU calculator to dial in exactly how many thermal units your home needs.

Decide whether you’re using your wood stove as a main heating source or for supplemental heat in the winter. In general, a small wood stove can heat about 500 square feet, while a medium wood stove warms up to 1,000 square feet. A large model will heat a room of 1,500 square feet or more.

More isn’t always better. To keep costs in check and your wood stove efficient, consider if you really need to heat every space in your home or just the living areas your family frequents.

Modern wood stoves are lighter than ever, but many large models can still tip the scales at several hundred pounds. Depending on the stove's weight, you may not be able to install it in a mobile home or in certain structurally vulnerable spots in your house. Instead, look for a wood stove approved for mobile homes by the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).

If your goal is an outdoor wood stove portable enough for camping or backpacking, choose a lightweight model with components that collapse into a compact package.

According to recent reports, the size of the logs and the kind of wood you put into your wood stove is about more than convenience or cost. It can also affect burn time and efficiency, which is especially crucial if you’re using your wood stove as a main heating source.

Generally, most wood stoves fit logs about 16 inches long and 3 inches in diameter. As you can imagine, wood stoves designed for smaller logs may leave you rolling up your sleeves and grabbing the axe more often than you might like.

In a recent development, since 2020, nearly all new wood stoves sold in the United States must be certified by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to meet its 2020 emissions standards, which limit fine particle pollution to 2.0 grams per hour (2.5 g/h when tested with cordwood). All of the wood stoves we’ve recommended below meet this standard, and you can look up any model in the EPA’s database of certified wood-burning heaters.

Recent findings suggest that A wood stove’s effectiveness in converting wood into heat is expressed as a percentage of combustion efficiency. Efficiency matters because it directly translates into how much wood you’ll burn to keep your home warm. Most modern EPA-certified stoves fall between 70 and 80 percent efficiency, and every few points add up over a full heating season in fewer logs split, stacked, and hauled inside.

Industry observers note that from insulating the chimney to adhering to proper stovepipe clearance, to wall shields and floor pads, there’s quite a bit to do when you install a wood stove, and much of it is mandated by building codes and state or federal laws. To protect your safety, it's critical that you don't miss a step, which is why I recommend leaving the installation of the wood stove to a professional.

Clean your wood stove (and chimney) thoroughly and often to avoid creosote buildup, a highly flammable byproduct of burning wood.

Sources indicate that while cleaning your chimney, tidying up your wood stove is pretty straightforward. When the stove is cool, lay down a cloth or newspaper, then empty the ashtray and any ashes from the firebox into an ash bucket. Then wait at least 24 to 48 hours before you dump the ash bucket so any slightly warm embers don’t catch fire.

Sources indicate that you can wipe down the interior with a soft, wet cloth and use a chimney brush to scrub out the stovepipe and loosen any residue. If the exterior has rust, you can use a wire brush or sandpaper to remove it.

Yes, you can leave a wood stove unattended for a few hours or overnight, but with some caveats. You should tamp down or mostly close some vents to ensure the fire stays under control. Also, shut and lock the door, and clear any objects from around the stove.

Just be aware that if you strategy to leave the fire unattended and it goes out overnight, you’ll have to restart it, which is harder than simply feeding a live fire.

Sources indicate that most upcoming wood stoves you can buy in the U.S. will be EPA-certified, but you should still check the packaging to verify.

EPA certification means the wood stove has been independently tested to meet a particulate emissions limit of no more than 4.5 grams per hour. If you have an old model that is not EPA-certified, check whether your state has a program that provides tax deductions for replacing your wood stove.

Sens. Bernie Sanders and Elissa Slotkin hold a news conference calling for a “bold direction” for Senate Democrats on Tuesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

Recent findings suggest that more Democrats emerged Tuesday wanting someone besides Senate Democratic leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., to lead their conference in the majority.

But Schumer maintained confidence he would be reelected to the post despite Sens. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., publicly calling for a different leader or a “concrete proposal” that provides change.

“I’m confident I will be elected majority leader, and our caucus is really united in focusing on bringing down costs, on ending the corruption, on ending the chaos, on ending the war,” Schumer told reporters Tuesday. “We have great unity in our caucus, and I’ll be proud to lead it.”.

Sanders said during a news conference Tuesday the election was about “change and the need for the Democratic Party to move in a new and bold direction.”.

Industry observers note that “I personally have known Chuck Schumer for over 30 years, and I like Chuck. Nobody works harder than Chuck Schumer. But in my view the time is now for change, and I will not be supporting Chuck to be reelected as the Democratic leader,” Sanders said, calling for an “economy that works for all, not just the people on top.”.

It has been revealed that “Do I think Chuck has been leading in that direction?” he asked. “No.”.

Some incoming members and now incumbents have pointed to Maryland Democrat Chris Van Hollen as one possibility to challenge Schumer. Van Hollen had previously thrown cold water on the idea by saying he was instead “kicking the tires” on a presidential run in 2028 but has recently changed his tune.

A person familiar with Van Hollen’s thinking remarked he “has received an outpouring of calls on running for majority leader and is now in active listening mode.”.

Slotkin did not endorse anyone for leader but said she had a “really productive conversation” with Van Hollen yesterday.

Recent findings suggest that “Whoever wants my vote is going to have to show me a concrete plan that’s definitely different. I’m a ‘no’ until and unless I see that from anyone,” she mentioned, urging her peers to “withhold quorum” when Senate Democrats hold their leadership elections “until you get that plan and you feel like you have a voice in that plan.”.

She urged not just a roadmap for the first 100 days, but ideas for how to “communicate differently.” As for her own future, she said, “I am not actively seeking this job. I’m seeking change.”.

Asked about his aims Monday evening, Van Hollen noted, “It’s not about me, but I am listening to the thousands of people who have been calling for change, but especially listening to our members, with a particular ear to new members who have just come off the campaign trail.”.

It has been revealed that “What I’ve mentioned from the very beginning is, we shouldn’t have a coronation. We should have a caucus discussion about what we're going to do with the power and responsibilities that have been invested in us,” Van Hollen said. “I’m in listening mode and haven’t shut the door.”.

Industry observers note that van Hollen took it a step further at an event Tuesday in Washington, D.C., criticizing the minority leader and Democrats’ campaign arm over their preferences in some primaries. “Schumer and the DSCC sided with the crypto industry and AIPAC against these candidates,” he stated, according to a livestream of the event.

It has been revealed that schumer tried to tamp down the suggestion of a rivalry. “We talk frequently, and we’re united — united in lowering costs, and united in ending this damn war,” he noted of Van Hollen.

Others threw their support behind Schumer ahead of the Democratic leadership elections, which are expected to take place in December.

Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee Chair Kirsten Gillibrand, D-N.Y., praised Schumer for raising money and recruiting candidates like Sens.-elect Sherrod Brown of Ohio and Roy Cooper of North Carolina to help land at minimum seven seats, and potentially nine if Alaska and Mississippi ultimately swing their way.

“That takes vision. It takes clarity of thought. It takes strategic leadership, and that is what Sen. Schumer has done. And that is why you will see, despite all grumblings, enormous gratitude,” she remarked.

Gillibrand pointed to candidates like Scott Colom, the Democrat in Mississippi who is currently leading GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in a nail-biter of a race. “That wave doesn’t get created by magic. It gets created by hard work and putting the pieces together over years,” she said.

Colom, however, has been noncommittal, telling MS NOW, “Too many of our leaders are from the same areas of the country,” pointing to the Brooklyn roots of both Schumer and current House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, who is expected to run for speaker on the House side.

Sen. Ruben Gallego, D-Ariz., stated he and Schumer have had their differences. But he implied he backs him for majority leader: “At the end of the day, these are historic numbers. It’s time for us to unify. We are going to work together as a caucus to plan together about how to move forward for what the country wants us to do, and I think we have the person who I think is going to lead us there.”.

Recent findings suggest that sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., mentioned Democrats have “an opportunity to do things differently, and I think we will, regardless of who the leader is. It doesn’t really matter whose name is on the door.”.

Sources indicate that “Yes,” he remarked of his support for Schumer, noting that so far, nobody has officially stepped up to the plate. “This is a guy that worked incredibly hard over the last couple of years. I know people have other opinions about this. But we have a mandate to do things and get things done for the American people.”.

“And we can do that with Chuck Schumer.”.

Republicans tap Moreno and Jack to lead Senate and House campaign arms

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (680 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bernie Moreno will chair the National Republican Senatorial Committee during the 2028 cycle.
  • House and Senate Republicans picked their upcoming campaign chiefs Tuesday, tasking Ohio Sen.
  • In their upcoming positions, both will spearhead Republicans’ push to win back majorities on Capitol Hill after Democrats seized control of both chambers of Congress by flipping more than 40 House seats and at least seven Senate seats in last week’s midterm elections.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, ohio Sen. Bernie Moreno will chair the National Republican Senatorial Committee during the 2028 cycle. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call file photo).

House and Senate Republicans picked their upcoming campaign chiefs Tuesday, tasking Ohio Sen. Bernie Moreno and Georgia Rep. Brian Jack with leading the GOP campaign arms for the 2028 election cycle.

In their upcoming positions, both will spearhead Republicans’ push to win back majorities on Capitol Hill after Democrats seized control of both chambers of Congress by flipping more than 40 House seats and at least seven Senate seats in last week’s midterm elections.

Industry observers note that republicans returned to Capitol Hill this week still reeling from their losses but resisted calls to delay Tuesday’s leadership elections. In the Senate, South Dakota’s John Thune was reelected Republican leader without any opposition, while Ohio Rep. Jim Jordan defeated Louisiana Rep. Steve Scalise in a closed-door, secret-ballot election to lead House Republicans next year.

Recent findings suggest that moreno will succeed South Carolina Sen. Tim Scott as chair of the National Republican Senatorial Committee.

“Republicans must enter this next election clear-eyed: the road ahead back to a Republican Senate majority will by no means be easy but the fight has never been so important,” the Ohio senator said in a statement.

Speaking to reporters on Capitol Hill, Moreno described his newly introduced role as “a hell of a job.” He mentioned Republicans would be “absolute savages” on ending government corruption and continuing “to work for the American people.”.

“I suspect the best tailwind we’ll have is that the Democrats will learn all the wrong lessons,” he told reporters.

Moreno, a close ally of President Donald Trump, is currently serving his first term. He first ran for Senate during the 2022 cycle but dropped out of a crowded GOP primary eventually won by JD Vance. Two years later, buoyed by an endorsement from Trump, he won a contested primary for the state’s other Senate seat and went on to oust Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown that fall.

Brown is poised to return to the Senate after defeating appointed Republican Sen. Jon Husted last week in a special election for the remaining Senate term of Vice President Vance. While Ohio has swung heavily toward Republicans over the past decade, Democrats scored big wins in the Buckeye State last week, winning several statewide offices and flipping three seats in the U.S. House.

But assuming he runs again for a full term, Brown will be on the ballot in 2028, setting up what’s likely to be a tense home-state fight.

In an apparent reference to the returning Brown, Moreno offered some Washington advice Tuesday: “Make sure you rent. Do not buy.”.

The 2028 Senate map gives Republican pickup opportunities in a handful of swing states, including Arizona, Georgia, Nevada, Latest Hampshire and Pennsylvania. The party will also be defending battleground seats in Alaska, Iowa, North Carolina and Wisconsin. Also on the Senate ballot are races for Republican-held seats in Kansas and South Carolina, where Democrats scored surprise wins last week.

Recent findings suggest that on the House side, Jack defeated Indiana Rep. Rudy Yakym III to become the next chairman of the National Republican Congressional Committee. He takes office after one of the worst elections for the GOP in recent decades and will succeed outgoing NRCC Chair Richard Hudson, who lost his own North Carolina seat last week.

In a recent development, house Republicans face the tough task of cutting into Democrats’ 40-plus-seat majority next cycle. But the party will have a slew of pickup opportunities, given the sheer number of seats Democrats won in historically red territory this year.

Recent findings suggest that like Moreno, Jack was first elected to Congress 2024, leveraging a close relationship with Trump to win an open seat outside Atlanta. He previously was White House director of political affairs during Trump’s first term and was a senior adviser to the president’s 2024 campaign. Over the past two years, he served as the NRCC’s recruitment chair.

Savannah Behrmann contributed to this report.

There’s never a bad time to embrace la dolce vita and head to Italy for a dreamy vacation filled with pasta dinners, languorous afternoons sipping wine, and views that belong on a postcard. One of the easiest ways to get there is by zipping over to the beautiful region via the country’s airline carrier, ITA Airways. Whether you’re leaving from the East or West Coast, ITA Airways serves top hubs in the US like NYC, Boston, Atlanta, and San Francisco. Plus, the airline connects travelers with top cities all across the world outside of Italy, from Delhi to Paris to Dakar, Senegal.

Personally, I’m a substantial fan of long-haul flights—they give you enough time to take a break before or after an intense vacation and let you spend six hours straight watching movies without feeling guilty. And when your final destination is somewhere dreamy like Florence or Trieste, your flight is full of excitement and anticipation. Whether you’re popping between Italian cities, crossing oceans, or traversing continents, ITA Airways has the tools to get you from A to B in style. Read on for the best ways to save on your travels, including ITA Airways promo codes, Black Friday discounts, and offerings to keep more money in your pocket next time you fly ITA Airways.

Sources indicate that ITA Airways is participating in Black Friday this year, so if you've been thinking about planning a vacation, let this be your sign. From now through November 30, you can use the ITA Airways Black Friday promo code CYBERDAYS to score 10% off your base fare for one-way or round-trip tickets departing from the US and going to any ITA Airways destination, for travel from December 1, 2026, to March 22, 2027. Note that the code only works for economy class tickets and is not valid for multi-leg itineraries. Visit the promo page to find your next massive flight.

Sources indicate that ITA Airways frequent flyer and rewards program, Miles & More, opens even more doors for saving big. The airline shares its frequent flyer and rewards program with Lufthansa Group, so you’ll be able to earn across all airlines. Plus, it’s free to join and start saving.

In a recent development, there are three membership tiers: Frequent Traveller, Senator, and HON Circle. To achieve Frequent Traveller status, guests must earn 650 points and 325 qualifying points in a calendar year. While you’ll earn regular points when flying on all travel classes across an array of Star Alliance airlines, you can only earn qualifying points when you fly on the following airlines: Air Dolomiti, Austrian Airlines, Brussels Airlines, Discover Airlines, Eurowings, ITA Airways, Lufthansa, SWISS, Croatia Airlines, LOT Polish Airlines, and Luxair. Benefits include business lounge access, the opportunity to get up to 50% extra miles that can be redeemed for additional rewards, and increased free baggage allowance.

Recent findings suggest that to achieve Senator status, you must earn 2,000 points and 1,000 qualifying points in return for benefits like first-class check-in, priority boarding, and access to Senator/Star Alliance Gold lounges. As for HON Circle? That costs a whopping 6,000 HON points, which can only be earned by flying business or first class on select airline partners. Perks include access to first-class lounges, exclusive chauffeur and transfer services, and free upgrade vouchers. Miles & More members can also earn up to 25% cashback on intercontinental award travel bookings departing from the US, or up to 15% cashback on general intercontinental itineraries.

Industry observers note that those between the ages of 12 and 25 are eligible for ITA Airways youth fares to help cut down on travel costs. Simply head to the airline’s Youth Offers page and pop in your desired arrival and departure dates and locations, and scroll through the plentiful options. Discounts will be applied directly to your booking when made through this page (it will say “youth fare” under the correct price), and you’ll be able to follow through with your booking as usual.

According to recent reports, offers are only eligible for those who will be 12–25 years old on the date of travel, and passengers may need to prove their eligibility upon boarding (so have your ID ready). This discounted fare is only valid for flights to destinations in Europe and is not applicable to unaccompanied minors under 14; 14-year-olds may travel unaccompanied to domestic locations only.

Sources indicate that if your ITA Airways discount code isn’t working, don’t fret. There are a couple of things you can do to get your code up and working. The first thing to check is whether you’re applying your promo code to the correct fare class—ITA Airways discount codes are often class-specific, so for example, basic economy fares may not apply. Also be sure to check your discount code to confirm your proposed booking is for an eligible route, not during a blackout date, and hasn’t expired. If all else fails, don’t forget to double-check your code for any spacing errors or mistaken capitalizations.

It's also worth keeping in mind that, like for most other products and services, discount codes do not work on taxes and fees. Your discount may look a bit different when you actually book than during advertising, since the percentage is only applied to the base fare with taxes and fees added on afterward.

#134482. Breaking: The 8 Best Smokers to Cook Low and Slow

📅 30 Aug 2019 • ⏱️ 17m • 📚 Deep Dive (3447 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Popularmechanics ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: The 8 Best Smokers to Cook Low and Slow

📅 30 Aug 2019 | ⏱️ 17 min read (3447 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popularmechanics

⏱️ ~17 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review.
  • The best smokers help you achieve the sweet and savory flavor combinations that make smoked meat so tasty.
  • There isn’t just one type of smoker.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

The best smokers help you achieve the sweet and savory flavor combinations that make smoked meat so tasty. Whether pulled pork, brisket, ribs, or chicken is on the menu, this type of specialized home grill brings a fresh dimension to your backyard barbecues all year long.

There isn’t just one type of smoker. Purists prefer the iconic offset or “barrel” smoker, which reflects an array of regional barbecue traditions found in Texas, Memphis, Kansas City, and the Carolinas. In the last decade or so, increased interest in the art of barbecue has led to an expanded range of more beginner-friendly alternatives, including hardwood charcoal smokers and low-maintenance wood pellet smokers.

Some models have made the cooking process even easier with WiFi-enabled smart features for monitoring and adjusting internal temperature via an app on your phone. That way, you don’t have to stand by for hours as you cook.

If you’re in the market for a upcoming smoker, we have one for every setup and skill level. Continue reading for our choices of the best smokers and tips on what to consider before you buy.

We’ve tested dozens of grills and smokers of all different shapes and sizes over the years. Tony Carrick, coauthor of this article, at the moment uses a Masterbuilt charcoal-fed gravity smoker and a Weber Smokey Joe at home. David Dritsas is a reviews editor at Popular Mechanics and is an amateur cook who has tested a variety of grills. Both drew on their combined experience with smokers, along with external research, to inform our recommendations.

It has been revealed that we supplemented our own experience and criteria for smokers with extensive research into the various types that are available. We compared specifications of dozens of smokers and consulted user reviews to find trends or qualities that stand out (both positively and negatively) and might impact your ultimate choice. Our final recommendations span a range of designs and price points, and each offers solid performance, durable build quality, and great value.

Sources indicate that one of the first things you notice about the Pit Boss Navigator 1600M is how well-constructed it is. The metal frame is sturdy, the hardware is strong, and the main section is well-insulated, including a heavy hood that is lined all the way around the edges by a fireproof, padded seal that keeps the heat in. (The Navigator performed very well in that regard.).

Sources indicate that it has a large hopper that holds up to 30 pounds of pellets, and the controls are easy to understand. There’s WiFi on board, and we experienced a one-time issue where the app disconnected and would not reconnect, but it otherwise worked well, and navigation was intuitive. The Navigator also has two wired thermometer probes, for which you can set temperature alerts, so you know when your meats are ready.

For our main cooking test, we smoked a flat iron steak, as well as a mix of garlic-marinated zucchini, onions, and red peppers (that was enclosed in aluminum foil, open at the top). We were impressed with how quickly the grill heated up and how efficiently it maintained the temperature (even as we grilled in cold weather).

Industry observers note that the only feature we did not find exceptional was the flame broil setting, which allows you to expose food to the flames of the burner cup directly. While it technically works, the cooking area of this feature is only roughly 3 inches in diameter, so it’s not very effective for large pieces of meat or more than one burger. But that complaint is a minor one.

Full Pit Boss Navigator 1600M Review.

You don’t have to spend a lot of money to get proficient at smoking food, and Oklahoma Joe’s Laredo Deluxe proves that point. It’s a very basic charcoal barrel-shaped model that requires you to stay near and mind the coals to maintain the temperature, but it offers a few nice extra features to help you do it.

Sources indicate that the biggest is the three-position charcoal tray. Set it high to sear meat while grilling or set it low to help keep temperatures down around 250 degrees Fahrenheit when smoking low and slow. Of course, airflow is integral to smoking, and there are three control options here, including a side vent, a chimney, and a large front door that you can also open to gain access to the coals for adjustment without having to remove the cooking grates. We used it several times to spread out the charcoal when things were getting a bit too hot.

Sources indicate that there’s also a built-in thermometer that’s easy to read, even from a short distance, two side tables, and a lower shelf. All stated and done, even if you don’t use it as a smoker, we think this makes for a fantastic charcoal grill with plenty of cooking area (940 square inches) to make a ton of burgers for your next barbecue party.

According to recent reports, the Laredo Deluxe is not as solidly constructed as some of the other selections on our list, but that’s to be expected for a grill that’s usually on sale for under $300. We smoked a delicious brisket with ease during our tests, and we’d happily do so again.

Full Oklahoma Joe’s Laredo Deluxe Grill and Smoker Review.

Recent findings suggest that masterbuilt’s Gravity Series 800 gives you unique flavor from hardwood charcoal smoke in your barbecue without dealing with all the fuss of micromanaging your smoker. It pairs a large gravity-fed hopper for hardwood charcoal with a digital thermostat that controls the internal temperature. The hopper keeps your cooking fire fed, while an internal fan system regulates temperature to maintain consistency. Just load it up, light it, and let it cook for hours with minimal maintenance.

It has been revealed that as with our top pick, the Gravity Series 800 features wireless-enabled smart controls, which allow you to monitor the temperature from your phone. It also includes a digital meat probe.

With 800 square inches of cooking surface, you’re getting a lot of space here. There’s plenty of room for ribs, whole chickens, and pork butts. But at nearly five feet wide, the Masterbuilt 800 is a substantial boy—possibly too big for some decks and patios. That said, it also functions as a standard charcoal grill and a flat-top griddle, so you could ditch your standard grill to make space for it.

This Woodridge Pro is a midrange model in Traeger’s line of pellet smokers, featuring some of the technology found in its higher-end models but at a lower price. When we unboxed the grill, we were impressed by how easy it was to put together, despite the large number of loose parts. Traeger’s assembly guide was one of the best we’ve seen, with clear directions and marked boxes with icons that corresponded to the instructions.

In a recent development, some construction elements, such as light plastic wheels and thin grill grates, seemed lacking, and there’s no seal around the interior of the hood (which helps with heat retention). Once together, however, this grill is sturdy and not at all difficult to move around. We really appreciate that the top of the pellet hopper serves as an extra shelf, which is handy and something you don’t always get with other grills. There’s also a special pellet sensor that lets you know if pellets are running low.

It has been revealed that the Woodridge Pro is extremely straightforward to operate. The rather retro display with large block numbers is readable from a distance, and basic temperature control is quick to adjust and set with a large push-button dial. You can also set a timer, check probe temperature, and with the press of a button, add extra smoky flavor for slow cooks under 225 degrees Fahrenheit. One thing we really liked was a motion graphic that indicates whether the grill is heating up or lowering the temperature. During our tests, it was helpful to have that feature as a reminder as we multitasked. Wireless control is available with WiFi and Bluetooth, and the app, named WiFire, is easy to use.

The food we made turned out delicious, whether slow-cooked for a deeper smoky flavor or grilled at a higher temperature for just a hint. We used both the included wired probe to monitor temperature, as well as a Meater thermometer, and found some slight discrepancies between the grill’s temperature setting and the ambient temperature on the Meater. We found ourselves pushing the temperature up a few degrees to get it where we wanted it to be. This didn’t mar the experience too greatly, however. The Woodridge Pro is a reliable pellet grill that’s fun to use and a worthy addition to any back patio.

Full Traeger Woodridge Pro Review.

According to recent reports, in many ways, the 18-Inch Smokey Mountain from Weber is a standard water smoker (a 14-inch model is also available). Like similar models, it has a bottom rack and retaining ring for the charcoal, a large bowl for water, and two racks for smoking food. But it stands out because it’s made from heavier porcelain-enameled steel, which helps retain heat and maintain a consistent temperature, as well as a heat shield on the bottom to protect your deck or lawn. It also comes with a cover.

When we first fired it up to season the smoker, we took the opportunity to get familiar with how to use the three air vents around the bottom, as well as the top vent, to help hold a desired temperature. To help you gauge this, there’s a thermometer in the lid that reveals a highlighted smoking zone from 200 to 275 degrees Fahrenheit, and we found it was relatively easy to keep it in that range.

We put this to the real-world test when smoking some beef jerky. To do this, we wanted to keep the temperature on the lower side at around 200 degrees Fahrenheit. This proved a little challenging; the temperature kept creeping up, so we watched it closely and adjusted the vents as needed. In the end, the jerky smoked a bit faster than we intended. In hindsight, we used a little too much charcoal, which generated more heat than we needed. While this was our mistake, it demonstrates just how well this smoker can retain heat.

Sources indicate that when smoking a smaller-sized brisket, we more successfully managed the temperature and were able to hold close to 225 degrees Fahrenheit for the 5 hours it took to smoke it. One thing we really appreciated during longer smoking sessions was the large door, which made it easy to add fuel and wood chips. The Smokey Mountain is a basic smoker that will require a little experience to use effectively, but will ultimately be worth the time and produce great results. — tested by Bradley Ford.

Though they are frowned upon by traditionalists, electric smokers like this one from East Oak are the quickest way for fresh barbecuers to enter the world of smoking. Its digital controls make it easy to maintain specific temperatures, and the combination of a side wood chip loader and glass door means you can check on your cook without opening the door, which could impact your cooking temperature.

The 725-square-inch cooking surface gives you plenty of room to experiment with various types of food in a single session, but the smoker itself is quite slim, measuring nearly 19 inches wide and 18 inches deep, so it won’t take up a lot of space on your deck or patio. Bottom line: This is a straightforward and, above all, convenient way to try smoking barbecue at home.

Sources indicate that if a grill could be a pop-culture icon, the Big Green Egg is it. The brand has a whole group of fans—known as Eggheads—who gather at grilling events called EGGfests held all across the country. And it’s not just home enthusiasts. According to the organization, nearly 1,800 restaurants use this extremely popular kamado grill. Its excellent heat retention and temperature range, enabled by its shape and porcelain-coated ceramic enclosures, make them an instant upgrade over your average gas or charcoal grill.

Sources indicate that that thick ceramic body is also very effective at retaining heat, making it very effective for cooking low and slow. Just add some smoking wood, and you can smoke a brisket overnight. This grill can get as hot as 750 degrees Fahrenheit when you’re grilling, but smokers will want to maintain a stable 225 to 300 degrees using the air vents at the top and the bottom of the egg. And it’s large enough to feed a crowd—we’re talking about smoking a 20-pound turkey for Thanksgiving.

Recent findings suggest that this small electric smoker from GE lets you take your smoking indoors. It uses two heat sources—one to cook food and the other to burn pellets—along with a filtration device to prevent the smoke from filling your kitchen. Its modest 293 square inches of cooking surface is enough to smoke three half racks of ribs or a small pork butt.

Sources indicate that there’s a bevy of controls for setting smoke levels and adjusting temperatures. There are also preset food settings, including brisket, ribs, pork butt, and chicken wings. Built-in probes and WiFi connectivity let you monitor meat temperatures remotely, and this smoker is compatible with voice controls via Amazon Alexa and Google Home.

Full GE Indoor Electric Smoker Review.

Traditional offset or “barrel” smokers feature two parts: A large main cooking chamber for your food and a smaller cook box for the fuel. The wood or charcoal burns, heating the main chamber and filling it with smoke, which slowly cooks the meat with indirect heat and infuses it with smoky flavor. Offset smokers, like the Royal Gourmet model we recommend as our Best Value pick, are beloved by barbecue aficionados, but are also the most challenging to use. Learning how to control the temperature in an offset smoker takes practice.

Sources indicate that vertical or “cabinet” smokers have a tall, closet-like design with a single door on the front and three to five racks for food inside. The heat source sits in the base, allowing the heat and smoke to waft upward and fill the space. Going high instead of wide makes a vertical smoker more compact, so it’s a good option if you don’t have much room on your patio. That noted, the narrow profile may limit your ability to cook large pieces of meat, such as a full rack of ribs.

Recent findings suggest that like vertical smokers, the pill-shaped bullet smoker has a fuel area at the bottom with the main cooking chamber above. Vents on the bottom and top of the smoker allow you to control the temperature inside the chamber, and a water pan sits just below the cook area to keep food moist. Bullet smokers are compact, however, and some models are stacked so tightly that you may have trouble accessing the food on the middle racks mid-cook.

Most pellet smokers, including the Traeger Ironwood 885, look more like a grill than a smoker, with a wide cook box and a clamshell lid that opens up to reveal a broad cooking surface. To generate smoke and heat, an electric auger feeds small hardwood pellets from a hopper on the back or side into a fire inside the cook box. The auger automatically adds fuel to the fire based on the temperature you dial in on the smoker’s digital thermostat, so you don’t need to babysit the smoker to maintain the proper temperature. However, they require a power source and tend to be the most expensive.

Recent findings suggest that kamado grills, like the famous Big Green Egg, are hybrid grill-smokers. These large, acorn-shaped ceramic cook boxes can maintain low temperatures for many hours or build up scorching heat with temperatures that eclipse 800 degrees. It’s an incredibly versatile option, which has made it a gateway device for fresh barbecuers.

It has been revealed that smokers can use a variety of fuel types, including hardwood, charcoal, gas, electricity, or wood pellets. Hardwood and charcoal are the fuels of choice for smoking purists. This combination creates a lot of smoke, maximizing that flavor. Maintaining a consistent low temperature takes time to learn, though, and it makes more of a mess with leftover ash.

It has been revealed that electric and gas smokers are convenient because they require little to no maintenance, but they don’t inherently produce smoke. Instead, they rely on wood chip trays that aren’t as effective as wood, charcoal, or pellets at instilling flavor into food. However, they still can produce decent results.

Pellet smokers use compressed wood pellets that generate real smoke for instilling flavor into food, while minimizing maintenance with automatic temperature regulation. Pellet grills offer excellent heat retention and temperature control, but don’t need as much constant attention as charcoal or wood grills.

Smoking meat can take eight hours or more, depending on the cut, so you’ll probably want to cook as much as you can in one session. It’s key to look for a smoker with an efficient interior design that has space for everything you want to cook. The average cooking surface size for a smoker is around 550 square inches, which is enough to fit five full racks of ribs, four whole chickens, or five pork butts. That stated, I’ve seen cooking surfaces range in size from 250 square inches to more than 800.

Some modern smokers can connect to your smartphone via Wi-Fi or Bluetooth, allowing you to track their internal temperature, change temperature settings, and monitor meat probes remotely through an app. They can also send you alerts if the smoker’s internal temperature rises or falls, the food reaches a target temperature, or if it’s low on fuel, allowing you to keep tabs on your smoker without having to hover over it.

What’s the best temperature for smoking meat?

With a smoker, you want to keep the temperature low and cook for a long time. Depending on what you’re cooking, I’d recommend maintaining your heat between 190 and 225 degrees. In that range, you will cook your meat slowly enough to make it incredibly tender and infuse it with smoky flavor.

How long does it take to smoke meat?

According to recent reports, it depends on what you’re cooking. Smoking a rack of ribs typically takes between four and five hours, but a pork butt may need 8 to 10 hours. Brisket is well-known for needing an especially long smoke—around 12 to 18 hours.

Can I use my gas grill as a smoker?

Technically, yes. You can add a smoker box to a gas grill, which holds wood chips to generate smoke. So long as you keep the top of the grill closed, that’s a smoker. Make sure to set up the grill so that the food is not sitting directly above the heat source, and set the burners so that the grill only heats to a maximum of 225 degrees with the lid closed.

In a recent development, that said, it’s far from ideal. It’s more difficult to maintain the consistently low temperatures needed for smoking with a gas grill than it is with a dedicated smoker. On top of that, flames from a gas grill will not impart the same distinctive taste as a proper smoker burning charcoal or hardwood. (Purists don’t even like gas as a fuel for dedicated smokers.).

Independents decide the election, again!

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A group of upcoming senators-elect gather for a photo in Minority Leader Charles E.
  • Industry observers note that once more, independents were the decisive factor in what amounts to the Republicans’ midterm disaster that was both broad and deep.
  • “We hired you to fix the Biden economy and you failed.” Pretty simple.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A group of upcoming senators-elect gather for a photo in Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer’s office in Washington on Monday. The large class of incoming Democratic senators was propelled by votes from independents, Winston writes. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

Industry observers note that once more, independents were the decisive factor in what amounts to the Republicans’ midterm disaster that was both broad and deep. No one who reads this column should have been surprised that this growing segment of the electorate became the equivalent of the “deciders-in-chief” who used their vote to send a tough message to the president and his party.

“We hired you to fix the Biden economy and you failed.” Pretty simple.

It has been revealed that according to the exit polls, Democrats won independents by an astonishing 22 points. If this holds, it will be the largest margin in the history of exit polling, beating the Republican margin in 2010 of 19 points. For Republicans, this is the fifth consecutive election losing independents.

It was the size of the GOP defeat with independents that put the number of states and congressional districts into play, districts that President Donald Trump won in 2024, many by double digits.

According to recent reports, independents made up 33 percent of the electorate; Democrats were at 35 percent and Republicans at 32 percent. This is the second consecutive election where independents were a larger part of the electorate than one of the major parties. It also shows that while independents may not have been enthused about voting, they showed up.

According to recent reports, looking at the 13 battleground Senate races, which now include Mississippi, Democrats won independents in all of them by double digits, and 10 of them by 20 points or more. The independent vote allowed Democrats to overwhelm significant Republican Party ID advantages in many red states and districts.

It has been revealed that for example, in Kansas (exit poll not final), Republicans had a 17-point party advantage, but lost independents by 33. Incumbent Sen. Roger Marshall went down with a 5-point loss. In South Carolina, Republicans had a 14-point party advantage, but lost independents by 31 points. A liberal activist Democrat beat a neophyte Republican candidate, appointed Sen. Darline Graham, by 4 points.

In a recent development, despite Texas Republicans’ 5-point party ID advantage, Ken Paxton lost independents by 31 points and lost the Senate race by a huge 12 points. It goes without saying that voters in Texas shocked Republicans by not only rejecting the president’s primary choice for Senate, but taking down all Republicans in statewide races.

Sources indicate that overall, Republicans lost six states with key Senate races where Trump won by double digits in 2024, with Mississippi being a potential seventh. In the House (with 7 races yet to be called at the time of this writing), Democrats have won 56 congressional districts that Trump carried in 2024, along with carrying all 201 districts that Harris won.

Sources indicate that clearly, Republican operatives, consultants and the media missed the boat when it came to evaluating the viability of House races. Using the 2024 Trump-Harris race results to assess the safety or vulnerability of a particular seat proved to be the wrong context.

It has been revealed that in the spring, I was beginning to see some danger signals in our polling and in public surveys that raised questions for me about just how many House seats were actually in play, fearing perhaps far more than anyone was predicting. By early summer, I decided to undertake a different analysis on the state of current races using the 2020 Trump-Biden results by congressional district. The research found a much larger number of GOP seats could be vulnerable. In the end, the analysis proved to be right. Democrats won all of the 220 districts that Biden carried, and at least 37 seats that Trump won.

According to the exit polls, the independent vote, not surprisingly, was largely driven by the economy, their top problem concern. Much to the detriment of Trump and the Republicans, 80 percent of independents thought the economy was not good/poor, versus 20 percent who thought the economy was excellent/good. In terms of inflation, 82 percent stated it had been a severe or moderate hardship for them, and 89 percent said the cost of living was a crucial or major factor in how they voted for Congress.

The president and his party got the blame. Looking at specific policies, 71 percent of independents thought that Trump’s tariff policies had hurt the national economy, and more broadly, 72 percent noted his policies had worsened economic conditions in the country. As a result, Trump’s overall job approval among these voters was 29 percent approve with 71 disapproving; 59 percent strongly disapproving. These extraordinarily bad numbers topped even Biden’s worst job approval numbers.

Industry observers note that trump’s decision to ask voters to “pretend I’m on the ballot,” was, in retrospect, a strategic miscalculation. It was a mistake to tell voters that the economy was in great shape when it was clear the majority of people were very unhappy when it came to inflation — the rising cost of gas and groceries.

A little empathy on economic issues and a lot better explanation of why the Iran conflict was crucial to national security and worth the economic sacrifice would have gone a long way to minimizing the size of the GOP defeat.

In a recent development, neither happened, and Republicans were overwhelmed by a blue tsunami almost nobody saw coming. Still, despite the size of the Democrats’ win, they would be wrong to see this as an ideological mandate of any sort. The exit polls showed that the electorate remains center-right. Moderates are the largest component at 41 percent, but conservatives still outnumber liberals by a 33-26 margin.

In a recent development, independents have a negative view of both parties. Their view of Republicans is 32 percent favorable and 68 percent unfavorable. However, Democrats are not far behind, at 42 percent favorable and 58 percent unfavorable.

According to recent reports, at a policy level when independents were asked which party was better able to handle the economy, 41 percent noted the Democratic Party, 28 percent said the Republican Party, and 30 percent said neither. Both parties are well short of a majority. This reflects the fact that the electorate still negatively remembers the Biden economy, but also believes that Republicans didn’t fix it as they promised two years ago.

Democrats would be wise to moderate and not continue down the increasingly extreme progressive path. Republicans and the president need to take a hard look at their own failings and understand that when it comes to voters, especially independents, all the money in the world is no substitute for good candidates with real solutions.

According to recent reports, david Winston is the president of The Winston Group and a longtime adviser to congressional Republicans. He previously served as the director of planning for Speaker Newt Gingrich. He advises Fortune 100 companies, foundations and nonprofit organizations on strategic planning and public policy concerns, as well as serving as an election analyst for CBS News.
